chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fell upon a man from the top of the house, so one of the two died. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is not upon the higher one anything, and there is not upon the lower one anything'.

key_terms.الْأَعْلَى: The one who fell from above
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: Anything (referring to blood money or compensation liability)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood money when one person falls on another and kills them accidentally?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of *diyah* (blood money) in cases of accidental death caused by falling, ruling that neither the person falling from above nor the one underneath bears financial liability. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *bara'ah asliyyah* (presumption of innocence/exemption from liability) in the absence of specific fault or negligence, distinguishing it from cases where one party's action directly caused the fall. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding liability in *qada'* (accidental) deaths within the framework of *fiqh*.
